Lobster is a c/7 diagonal spaceship that was discovered by Matthias Merzenich on August 19, 2011. It was the first c/7 diagonal spaceship to be found. It consists of two gliders pulling a tagalong-like object that then rephases them. It can be infinitely extended.

Lobster (spaceship) was voted Pattern of the Year for 2011 on the ConwayLife.com forums, tied with the fully universal Turing machine.

7016.d: This cosmic work of art is like a glimpse of photons floating around in an endless entropy. The magic of light and colour is that we can never truly describe it as we all perceive it differently. No one really knows if blue is blue or green is green or if a bee sees the same yellow on a sunflower as we do. The strange satisfaction of watching patterns emerge and simultaneously disappear tingles our brain cells. As the rings form around the centre, does it remind you of a distant childhood memory? Perhaps a long-standing mental image that you can neither erase nor decipher? Are these organisms as seen through a microscope or the iris of an eye that mimics a nebula? It can also be intriguing that it looks like a black hole. Imagine, you were standing beyond the event horizon of this black hole, what wonders would you find? Does it feel like a dense web of space and time? One piece of art can be viewed from a million perspectives, and these are just mine. Interesting isn't it?

A multimedia NFT that generates a unique beat and a rotative sandbox. Then you start beats and sand grains will explode & more & change colors according to real sound waves.

You can pause, restart, increase number of sand grains up to 4M and resolution up to 4K.

If you like rotosandbeats, check this too https://www.fxhash.xyz/generative/slug/sandbeats-diptych-2

WARNING: Webgl/GPU compliant, CPU compliant but might lag, runs on mobile but lags a lot.

Controls:
- H: hide/show help.
- Dbl-Click - Space: start/pause animation for snapshots.
- S - Z/W: particles more/less (256^2, 512^2, 1024^2, 2048^2).
- Q/A - D: resolution down/up (720p, 1080p, 2K, 4K, 8K).
- R: restart animation from scratch.
- I: hide/show info panel. Click for panels (info, FPS).

RotoSandBeats @naibdian 2021 using Opensource WebGL, ReactJS, ThreeJS libs.

This token is GPU intensive, viewing on desktop is recommended.

Press “UP” or “DOWN” to increase or decrease the number of simulated rays per pixel, this will have an impact on performance.

Time Pieces is a series that explores the roll time can play in a work of art. Specifically, how can I use time within a piece to help me tell a deeper story and (hopefully) provide a richer experience for the viewer?  

"Day and Night" is a first attempt in this exploration. 

The piece is constructed of 40, randomly colored shapes that together form a seated female nude.  Some (rather few) pieces will be signed.  Time has been added to created two views of the piece: 

- The "day" view can be seen when viewing the piece between 7:00 AM and 7:00 PM
- The "night" view can be seen when viewing the piece between 7:00 PM and 7:00 AM

These times are local to the viewer.
To view each mode, open the live view at the appropriate time.

7123.d:
Ambient Landscapes is an audiovisual modular synthesizer.

Each edition has unique base sequence, scale, parameter combination, and visual landscape.

The generation principle is based on aliasing technique - a base sequence is modulated to hearable range, then passed through an effect chain and demodulated back to a sequence. Passed through quantizer this gives an almost infinite continuous field of base melody variations, completely controllable by parameters of the effect chain. Besides that, one also can control pitch, tempo, noise amount, filters and shape of the second melody by dragging the stars in the constellations. Each star can also be toggled to drift and evolve in automatic mode.

Interface:
- click / space to start
- mouse to drag dots and change params
- "e" while dragging to toggle dot auto evolution
- "v" to unfold to full screen (also gives better performance)
- "r" to reset dots to initial positions

Engine: @ferluht
Generative patch design: @alexeev

A simple black, white, and red palette is chosen to not distract from the beauty of these curves.

An endless flow of particles draws a flower. Their paths are guided by the color values of an input image. One of the parameters in the system varies slowly over time, so the behavior of the particles changes. The digital painting on the screen, like a visualization of the swarm's behavior, shifts as well. Old strokes fade into black, constantly replaced by new ones.

Each piece takes as input one of 16 different photos of flowers I took during a trip through Salta and Jujuy provinces in the Argentinean North-West (NOA): a dry, rugged, and very beautiful part of the country I live in.

Controls:
[SPACE] to pause / play. 
[s] to save image capture

This work is part of the “Dreamlines” series of explorations on algorithmic redrawings of images, which started more than 15 years ago and has had many iterations.

w=stat(6)s=1

end
srand(s)

poke(z,0x00)
for y=0,d do
pset(r(g),r(g),(1+f(r(3)))+3*p)end
sspr(0,0,g,g,a,a,g-a*2,g-a*2)
poke(z,0x60)
